name: Phoenix livery
description: White, with two straight blue lines along the fuselage: a thin one just under the windows and a broader band below it, both running from the nose to the tail cone. White fin with the red phoenix (the same artwork on both sides, so it faces aft on the right). Up front, the Chinese flag, 'AIR CHINA' in black italic capitals and '中国国际航空公司' in black brush calligraphy; a Star Alliance badge behind the cockpit; small phoenixes on the winglets.

areas.name: thin blue line under the windows
blue band, nose to tail cone

logos.description: The phoenix: a red bird drawn in a few calligraphic strokes, a small crested head with a beak on one side at mid-height, a U-shaped body stroke curving under, and three long feathers sweeping up and away to the opposite top corner, the middle one curling into a spiral. Its strokes also read as the letters 'VIP'. On the left the head faces the nose; the right side shows the same artwork, head aft.
The phoenix, small, near the winglet's tip.
The flag of the People's Republic of China: red, one large and four small yellow stars at the hoist's top corner; ahead of 'AIR CHINA' on both sides.
The Star Alliance star: a small gray five-pointed star of five wedge shapes, just behind the cockpit windows.

titles.style: Heavy italic capitals, geometric, the A drawn as a pointed arch; behind the flag.

similar: ITC Avant Garde Gothic Bold Oblique

titles.style: Brush calligraphy (Deng Xiaoping's hand), widely spaced over the windows aft of 'AIR CHINA'; on the right side it reads left to right, starting aft.

notes: Measured on the A321neo (B-32CC, left side); the A350 and 787 carry the same layout. The lower fuselage looks a little grayer than the crown in sunlit photos; taken as white shading, not checked from below. On the right side the order from the nose is the same (flag, AIR CHINA, Chinese), so the Chinese there reads left to right from aft. A small type name ('AIRBUS A321neo') sits aft under the band, not drawn. Colors by eye except the flag. Re-checked 2026-11-15 on the 737-800 (the commonest type, B-5447 from the right): AIR CHINA runs 0.20 to 0.285 with the flag just ahead of it, the Chinese name 0.30 to 0.49 (on the A321neo they sat at 0.16 and 0.25).
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximation. The phoenix and this white scheme with blue lines date from Air China's creation as the flag carrier's brand (1988); the introduction year of the present cheatline isn't confirmed here, so `from` is left out.
